mechanism_narrative: Sustained week-on-week improvement in RETAIL_REC (from -27.3% to -4.1%) over the past three weeks indicates a monotonic recovery trend. This trend will persist over the next four weeks, driving RETAIL_REC to remain higher than the baseline mean of the last 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 23.2 percentage points over three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days falls below the mean of -13.5% (average of t-3w through t-0w).

mechanism_narrative: Rising GROCERY_PHARM mobility (from -9.0% to +11.3%) signals increased essential-trip frequency and consumer confidence. This behavioral shift toward essential commerce will spill over into discretionary retail visits within the next two weeks, elevating RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at +11.3% in t-0w, highest in snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase week-on-week in at least two of the next four weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining above +5%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility remains severely depressed (t-0w: -13.1%) but is recovering (from -38.4%). When TRANSIT recovers to within 10 percentage points of baseline, commuting resumes and retail footfall during commute windows increases. This mechanism activates only when TRANSIT crosses -10%.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 25.3 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT remains below -10% for all four weeks ahead, and RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility remains elevated (68.3% at t-0w) while WORKPLACES remain depressed (-19.7%). This divergence indicates outdoor leisure substitution for indoor work. If WORKPLACES does not recover to within -10% of baseline within one week, outdoor-leisure preference will suppress retail-and-recreation visits, driving RETAIL_REC lower.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -10% AND PARKS remains above +50%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases week-on-week in the next week despite WORKPLACES staying below -10% and PARKS remaining above +50%.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility is declining (from +4.7% to +1.4%), indicating reduced home-confinement behavior. Combined with rising GROCERY_PHARM (+11.3%), this signals confidence to venture outside. The interaction of declining RESIDENTIAL and rising GROCERY_PHARM will drive RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the last 28-day mean, or RESIDENTIAL rebounds above +3% while GROCERY_PHARM falls below +8%.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has stabilized at -19.7% (minimal change from -20.6% in t-1w), indicating a policy-imposed or structural ceiling on workplace return. This stalled recovery signals ongoing restrictions that will constrain RETAIL_REC growth, preventing it from exceeding the last 28-day mean.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES week-on-week change is less than 2 percentage points
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES changed only 0.9 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES recovers more than 5 percentage points in any single week ahead, and RETAIL_REC simultaneously increases above the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility at +68.3% indicates strong seasonal outdoor preference (consistent with t-1w: +72.1%). This seasonal peak will persist for one more week before declining, and the decline will coincide with a shift of leisure visits from parks to indoor retail, raising RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines more than 5 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined 3.8 points from t-1w to t-0w, indicating early seasonal reversal
failure_condition: PARKS continues to rise or remain flat in the next week, and RETAIL_REC does not increase week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT recovery (from -38.4% to -13.1%) combined with WORKPLACES stabilization (at -19.7%) indicates a bifurcated labor market: some workers commuting, others remote. This partial commute recovery will drive retail visits near transit hubs within two weeks, but the effect will be limited by the persistent workplace deficit, resulting in modest RETAIL_REC gains.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves more than 5 points week-on-week AND WORKPLACES remains between -25% and -15%
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 7.9 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase in at least two of the next four weeks, or WORKPLACES falls below -25% while TRANSIT continues recovering.
